# {project_name} - Design Spec

## I. Project Information

| Item | Value |
| ---- | ----- |
| **Project Name** | {project_name} |
| **Canvas Format** | {canvas_info['name']} ({canvas_info['dimensions']}) |
| **Page Count** | [Filled by Strategist] |
| **Design Style** | {design_style} |
| **Target Audience** | [Filled by Strategist] |
| **Use Case** | [Filled by Strategist] |
| **Created Date** | {date_str} |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
| -------- | ----- |
| **Format** | {canvas_info['name']} |
| **Dimensions** | {canvas_info['dimensions']} |
| **viewBox** | `{canvas_info['viewbox']}` |
| **Margins** | [Recommended by Strategist, e.g., left/right 60px, top/bottom 50px] |
| **Content Area** | [Calculated from canvas] |

---

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Style**: {design_style}
- **Theme**: [Light theme / Dark theme]
- **Tone**: [Filled by Strategist, e.g., tech, professional, modern, innovative]

### Color Scheme

> Strategist should determine specific color values based on project content, industry, and brand colors

| Role | HEX | Purpose |
| ---- | --- | ------- |
| **Background** | `#......` | Page background (light theme typically white; dark theme dark gray/navy) |
| **Secondary bg** | `#......` | Card background, section background |
| **Primary** | `#......` | Title decorations, key sections, icons |
| **Accent** | `#......` | Data highlights, key information, links |
| **Secondary accent** | `#......` | Secondary emphasis, gradient transitions |
| **Body text** | `#......` | Main body text (dark theme uses light text) |
| **Secondary text** | `#......` | Captions, annotations |
| **Tertiary text** | `#......` | Supplementary info, footers |
| **Border/divider** | `#......` | Card borders, divider lines |
| **Success** | `#......` | Positive indicators (green family) |
| **Warning** | `#......` | Issue markers (red family) |

> **Reference**: Industry colors in `references/strategist.md` or `scripts/config.py` under `INDUSTRY_COLORS`

### Gradient Scheme (if needed, using SVG syntax)

```xml
<!-- Title gradient -->
<linearGradient id="titleGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#[primary]"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#[secondary accent]"/>
</linearGradient>

<!-- Background decorative gradient (note: rgba forbidden, use stop-opacity) -->
<radialGradient id="bgDecor" cx="80%" cy="20%" r="50%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#[primary]" stop-opacity="0.15"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#[primary]" stop-opacity="0"/>
</radialGradient>
```

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Plan

> Strategist should select a font preset based on content characteristics, or customize the font combination
> Preset descriptions: P1=Modern business/tech | P2=Government docs | P3=Culture/arts | P4=Traditional/conservative | P5=English-primary

**Recommended preset**: [Fill in preset code]

| Role | Chinese | English | Fallback |
| ---- | ------- | ------- | -------- |
| **Title** | [font name] | [font name] | [font name] |
| **Body** | [font name] | [font name] | [font name] |
| **Code** | - | Consolas | Monaco |
| **Emphasis** | [font name] | [font name] | [font name] |

**Font stack**: `[Fill in CSS font-family string]`

### Font Size Hierarchy

> **Design principle**: Use body font size as baseline (1x), derive other levels proportionally
> **Unit convention**: Use px uniformly (SVG native unit) to avoid pt/px conversion errors
> **Selection principle**: Font size is based on **content density**, not design style

**Baseline**: Body font size = [fill in]px (choose 18-24px based on content density)

| Purpose | Ratio | 24px baseline (relaxed) | 18px baseline (dense) | Weight |
| ------- | ----- | ---------------------- | -------------------- | ------ |
| Cover title | 2.5-3x | 60-72px | 45-54px | Bold |
| Chapter title | 2-2.5x | 48-60px | 36-45px | Bold |
| Content title | 1.5-2x | 36-48px | 27-36px | Bold |
| Subtitle | 1.2-1.5x | 29-36px | 22-27px | SemiBold |
| **Body content** | **1x** | **24px** | **18px** | Regular |
| Annotation | 0.75-0.85x | 18-20px | 14-15px | Regular |
| Page number/date | 0.55-0.65x | 13-16px | 10-12px | Regular |

> **Tip**: Dense content (6+ points per page) use 18px; relaxed content (3-5 points per page) use 24px

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

- **Header area**: [Height and content description]
- **Content area**: [Height and content description]
- **Footer area**: [Height and content description]

### Common Layout Modes

| Mode | Suitable Scenarios |
| ---- | ----------------- |
| **Single column centered** | Covers, conclusions, key points |
| **Left-right split (5:5)** | Comparisons, dual concepts |
| **Left-right split (4:6)** | Image-text mix |
| **Top-bottom split** | Processes, timelines |
| **Three/four column cards** | Feature lists, team introductions |
| **Matrix grid** | Comparative analysis, classifications |

### Spacing Specification

> Strategist may adjust based on project needs

| Element | Recommended Range | Current Project |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| Card gap | 20-32px | [fill in] |
| Content block gap | 24-40px | [fill in] |
| Card padding | 20-32px | [fill in] |
| Card border radius | 8-16px | [fill in] |
| Icon-text gap | 8-16px | [fill in] |
| Single-row card height | 530-600px | [fill in] |
| Double-row card height | 265-295px each | [fill in] |
| Three-column card width | 360-380px each | [fill in] |

---

## VI. Icon Usage Specification

### Source

- **Built-in icon library**: `templates/icons/` (640+ icons)
- **Usage method**: Placeholder format `{{icon:category/icon-name}}`

### Recommended Icon List (fill as needed)

| Purpose | Icon Path | Page |
| ------- | --------- | ---- |
| [example] | `{{icon:interface/check-circle}}` | Slide XX |

---

## VII. Chart Reference List (if needed)

> When the presentation includes data visualization, Strategist selects chart types from `templates/charts/charts_index.json` and lists them here for the Executor to reference.

| Chart Type | Reference Template | Used In |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------- |
| [e.g. grouped_bar_chart] | `templates/charts/grouped_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 05 |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List (if needed)

| Filename | Dimensions | Ratio | Purpose | Type | Status | Generation Description |
| -------- | --------- | ----- | ------- | ---- | ------ | --------------------- |
| cover_bg.png | {canvas_info['dimensions']} | [ratio] | Cover background | [Background/Photography/Illustration/Diagram/Decorative] | [Pending/Existing/Placeholder] | [AI generation prompt] |

**Status descriptions**:

- **Pending** - Needs AI generation, provide detailed description
- **Existing** - User already has image, place in `images/`
- **Placeholder** - Not yet processed, use dashed border placeholder in SVG

**Type descriptions** (used by Image_Generator for prompt strategy selection):

- **Background** - Full-page background for covers/chapters, reserve text area
- **Photography** - Real scenes, people, products, architecture
- **Illustration** - Flat design, vector style, cartoon, concept diagrams
- **Diagram** - Flowcharts, architecture diagrams, concept maps
- **Decorative** - Partial decorations, textures, borders, dividers

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: [Chapter Name]

#### Slide 01 - Cover

- **Layout**: Full-screen background image + centered title
- **Title**: [Main title]
- **Subtitle**: [Subtitle]
- **Info**: [Author / Date / Organization]

#### Slide 02 - [Page Name]

- **Layout**: [Choose layout mode]
- **Title**: [Page title]
- **Chart**: [chart_type] (see VII. Chart Reference List)
- **Content**:
  - [Point 1]
  - [Point 2]
  - [Point 3]

> **Chart field**: Only add when the page includes data visualization. Chart type must be listed in section VII.

---

[Strategist continues adding more pages based on source document content and page count planning...]

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

Generate corresponding speaker note files for each page, saved to the `notes/` directory:

- **File naming**: Match SVG names, e.g., `01_cover.md`
- **Content includes**: Script key points, timing cues, transition phrases

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Must Follow:

1. viewBox: `{canvas_info['viewbox']}`
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` (`<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN)
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`; `rgba()` FORBIDDEN
5. FORBIDDEN: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. FORBIDDEN: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Arrows use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>`

### PPT Compatibility Rules:

- `<g opacity="...">` FORBIDDEN (group opacity); set on each child element individually
- Image transparency uses overlay mask layer (`<rect fill="bg-color" opacity="0.x"/>`)
- Inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` FORBIDDEN

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-generation

- [ ] Content fits page capacity
- [ ] Layout mode selected correctly
- [ ] Colors used semantically

### Post-generation

- [ ] viewBox = `{canvas_info['viewbox']}`
- [ ] No `<foreignObject>` elements
- [ ] All text readable (>=14px)
- [ ] Content within safe area
- [ ] All elements aligned to grid
- [ ] Same elements maintain consistent style
- [ ] Colors conform to spec
- [ ] CRAP four-principle check passed

---

## XIII. Next Steps

1. ✅ Design spec complete
2. **Next step**: [Choose based on image approach]
   - No AI images → Invoke **Executor** role to generate SVGs
   - Has AI images → Invoke **Image_Generator** role, then invoke Executor after completion

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Style**: Top Consulting / Exhibit
- **Theme**: Hybrid — dark cover/chapter pages + light content pages

### Color Scheme

| **Content Background** | `#FFFFFF` | Content page main background |

| **Gradient End** | `#1E40AF` | Top gradient bar end (deep blue) |

| **Dark Takeaway Bar** | `#1F2937` | Exhibit-style key message bar background |

<!-- Dark page background radial accent -->

  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#00796B" stop-opacity="0.12"/>

## IV. Typography System

**Recommended preset**: P5 (English-primary)

### Font Size Hierarchy

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

| ---------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------- |

| `grouped_bar_chart` | `templates/charts/grouped_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 04 | Side-by-side depression vs anxiety DALY comparison |
| `kpi_cards` | `templates/charts/kpi_cards.svg` | Slide 02 | Large callout numbers (1 in 3 women, 1 in 5 men) |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List

No images required — data-forward report style. All visuals are constructed via SVG chart templates and icon library.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: Overview

#### Slide 01 — Cover

- **Layout**: Dark background, centered title block, decorative elements
- **Page type**: Cover (01_cover.svg template)
- **Title**: The Global Burden of Mental Illness: Prevalence, Impact, and the Treatment Gap
- **Subtitle**: Global Data | 2023 | IHME Global Burden of Disease
- **Attribution**: Source: Our World in Data — Dattani, Rodés-Guirao, Ritchie & Roser (2023) / IHME GBD 2025
- **Date**: April 2026
- **Bottom label**: CONFIDENTIAL (gold, centered)

#### Slide 02 — Scale of Mental Illness

- **Layout**: Large callout numbers (KPI-style) top section + supporting text block below
- **Key message bar**: "Hundreds of Millions Affected — Mental Illness Is a Universal Burden"
- **Callouts**:
  - "1 in 3" + label "women will experience major depression in their lifetime"
  - "1 in 5" + label "men will experience major depression in their lifetime"
- **Supporting text**: Mental health conditions span from common (depression, anxiety) to less prevalent but severe (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder). Hundreds of millions suffer each year; many more over their lifetimes.
- **Icon**: `users` (top left of callout)
- **Footer source**: Our World in Data / IHME GBD 2025

#### Slide 03 — Burden by Category (Central Data Slide)

- **Layout**: Full-content area horizontal bar chart
- **Chart**: `horizontal_bar_chart` — 5 categories
- **Key message bar**: "Depression and Anxiety Dominate — ~695 and ~687 DALYs per 100K Respectively"
- **Chart data** (DALYs per 100,000, World 2023):
  - Depressive disorders: 694.6 (chart bar color: `#1E40AF`)
  - Anxiety disorders: 686.5 (chart bar color: `#00796B`)
  - Schizophrenia: 210.2 (chart bar color: `#475569`)
  - Bipolar disorder: 94.6 (chart bar color: `#9CA3AF`)
  - Eating disorders: 47.5 (chart bar color: `#CBD5E1`)
- **Annotation**: DALYs = Disability-Adjusted Life Years per 100,000 people. Source: IHME GBD 2025
- **Note**: Values are exact from source_brief.md — do not modify

#### Slide 04 — Depression vs Anxiety Parity

- **Layout**: Left-right split (5:5) with two large paired bar visuals + text annotation
- **Chart**: `grouped_bar_chart` — 2-series (Depression vs Anxiety), single data point each
- **Key message bar**: "Depression and Anxiety Carry Nearly Equal Disease Burden Worldwide"
- **Left bar**: Depressive Disorders — 694.6 DALYs/100K (color `#1E40AF`)
- **Right bar**: Anxiety Disorders — 686.5 DALYs/100K (color `#00796B`)
- **Annotation panel**: Together they account for ~80% of the total mental health disease burden across the five main categories — dwarfing all other conditions combined.
- **Difference callout**: Difference of only 8.1 DALYs/100K — statistically near-identical
- **Footer source**: IHME GBD 2025

#### Slide 05 — Severe Conditions: Lower Prevalence, High Individual Impact

- **Layout**: Two-column comparison cards
- **Key message bar**: "Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder: Lower Prevalence, Severe Individual Impact"
- **Left card (Schizophrenia)**:
  - Headline: 210.2 DALYs per 100,000
  - Body: While schizophrenia affects fewer people at the population level, it generates 210.2 DALYs/100K — reflecting profound disability, early onset, and lifetime severity.
  - Contrast note: ~30% of the depression/anxiety burden, but concentrated in a smaller, severely impaired group
- **Right card (Bipolar Disorder)**:
  - Headline: 94.6 DALYs per 100,000
  - Body: Bipolar disorder contributes 94.6 DALYs/100K. Episodes of extreme mood disruption significantly impair occupational and social functioning even between acute phases.
  - Contrast note: ~14% of the depression/anxiety burden
- **Bottom comparison bar**: Visual proportion strip showing all 5 categories
- **Footer source**: IHME GBD 2025

#### Slide 06 — The Treatment Gap

- **Layout**: Icon-driven infographic grid (2×2 barriers)
- **Key message bar**: "Treatment Is Available but Often Lacking or of Poor Quality"
- **Opening statement**: Mental illnesses are treatable. Yet a large treatment gap persists — particularly in low- and middle-income countries.
- **Four barrier cards** (icon + heading + 1-line body):
  1. `triangle-exclamation` — **Stigma**: Many people are uncomfortable disclosing symptoms to healthcare professionals or those they know.
  2. `lock-closed` — **Access Barriers**: Treatment is often lacking, especially in low- and middle-income countries.
  3. `shield` — **Quality Gaps**: Even where treatment exists, it may be of poor quality.
  4. `magnifying-glass` — **Underreporting**: Discomfort with disclosure makes it difficult to estimate true prevalence — the actual burden may be higher than reported.
- **Footer source**: Our World in Data / IHME GBD 2025

#### Slide 07 — How People Cope

- **Layout**: Three-column icon card grid
- **Key message bar**: "How People Cope: From Medication to Faith to Family Conversations"
- **Intro line**: Global survey data reveals wide variation in how people deal with anxiety or depression.
- **Three coping strategy cards**:
  1. `pills` — **Prescribed Medication** — Common in higher-income settings; the biomedical pathway. Access varies widely by country income level.
  2. `heart` — **Religious or Spiritual Activities** — Prevalent in many regions worldwide; reflects cultural and community-level coping frameworks.
  3. `person` — **Talking to Friends or Family** — A widely reported coping mechanism across all settings; underscores the role of social support networks.
- **Insight box**: The diversity of coping strategies underscores that mental health responses are shaped by cultural, economic, and healthcare system factors. Policy interventions must account for these differences.
- **Footer**: Source: Our World in Data (Global Survey Data); figure_2 reference

#### Slide 08 — Key Takeaways and Policy Implications

- **Layout**: Structured bullet list with numbered callout icons
- **Page type**: Ending/conclusion
- **Key message bar**: "Key Takeaways: Prioritizing Depression, Anxiety, and Closing the Treatment Gap"
- **Five takeaways** (each with `circle-checkmark` icon):
  1. Depression and anxiety together represent the overwhelming majority of mental health DALYs — ~695 and ~687 per 100K respectively, each nearly equal in burden.
  2. Schizophrenia and bipolar disorder carry disproportionate individual burden relative to prevalence — specialized care must be maintained.
  3. Effective treatments exist, but access and quality remain inadequate — especially in low- and middle-income countries.
  4. Stigma suppresses both help-seeking behavior and accurate epidemiological data — the true burden is likely underestimated.
  5. Policy should prioritize scaling evidence-based interventions for common mental disorders (depression, anxiety) while preserving specialized care for severe conditions.
- **Bottom CTA**: Data source: Our World in Data / IHME Global Burden of Disease 2025

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

- **File naming**: Match SVG names — `01_cover.md`, `02_mental_health_scale.md`, etc.
- **Total duration**: ~15 minutes (≈2 min per slide for policy briefing)
- **Notes style**: Formal / evidence-based
- **Presentation purpose**: Inform + Persuade
- **Content structure**: Key talking point → supporting data → transition to next slide

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Rules:

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720` — mandatory on every SVG
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` — `<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` — `rgba()` FORBIDDEN
5. FORBIDDEN: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. FORBIDDEN: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Arrows use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>`
8. Gradients defined in `<defs>` with `<linearGradient>`

### PPT Compatibility Rules:

- `<g opacity="...">` FORBIDDEN — set opacity on each individual child element
- Inline styles only — no external CSS, no `@font-face`

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-generation

- [x] Content fits page capacity (max 6 items per content page)
- [x] All DALY figures verified against source_brief.md
- [x] No fabricated statistics — all data from source material only
- [x] Layout mode selected for each slide
- [x] Icon inventory verified against icons_index.json

### Post-generation

- [ ] viewBox = `0 0 1280 720` on all SVGs
- [ ] No `<foreignObject>` elements
- [ ] All text >= 13px (readable)
- [ ] Content within safe area (x: 40–1240, y: 20–680)
- [ ] Consistent styling across same-type elements
- [ ] Colors conform to spec above
- [ ] Footer on every content slide

---

## XIII. Next Steps

1. ✅ Design spec complete — no AI image generation needed
2. **Next step**: Invoke **Executor** role (Top Consulting style: `executor-base.md` + `executor-consultant-top.md`)

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

1	# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>

62

88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤

94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤

97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │

101	```
102

104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106

108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```

115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117

119

121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|
128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight

129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132	
133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
138	
139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Speaker Notes Style
151	
152	### Narrative Tone
153	
154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
155	
156	### Stage Direction Markers
157	
158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
159	|--------|---------|---------|
160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
165	
166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
167	
168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`
173	
174	### Notes Example
175	
176	```markdown
177	# 03_strategic_path
178	
179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
180	
181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
182	
183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
185	
186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
188	
189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
190	
191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
192	Duration: 3 minutes
193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
194	```
195	
196	---
197	
198	## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement
199	
200	### Content Level
201	
202	- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
203	- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
204	- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
205	- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
206	
207	### Visual Level
208	
209	- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
210	- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout
213	
214	### Notes Level
215	
216	- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
218	- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration
219

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#00796B"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="url(#topGrad)"/>

  <!-- Exhibit Takeaway Bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="1200" height="58" fill="#0D1117" rx="2"/>
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="5" height="58" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="58" y="51" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" letter-spacing="0.5">Hundreds of Millions Affected — Mental Illness Is a Universal Burden Spanning the Globe</text>

  <!-- Section intro line -->
  <text x="40" y="100" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">Key lifetime prevalence estimates  ·  Source: Our World in Data / IHME GBD 2025</text>

  <!-- Divider under intro -->
  <line x1="40" y1="112" x2="1240" y2="112" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- LEFT CALLOUT — 1 in 3 Women -->
  <rect x="40" y="128" width="570" height="360" fill="#F0FDF4" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="128" width="5" height="360" fill="#00796B" rx="2"/>

  <!-- Icon placeholder -->
  <use data-icon="users" x="60" y="145" width="32" height="32" fill="#00796B"/>

  <text x="65" y="185" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#00796B" letter-spacing="1">WOMEN</text>

  <!-- Big callout number -->
  <text x="300" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="128" font-weight="bold" fill="#00796B" fill-opacity="0.15">3</text>
  <text x="90" y="295" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="76" font-weight="bold" fill="#0D1117">1 in 3</text>

  <text x="60" y="342" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#374151">women will experience</text>
  <text x="60" y="368" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#00796B">major depression</text>
  <text x="60" y="394" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#374151">in their lifetime</text>

  <rect x="60" y="420" width="520" height="1" fill="#D1FAE5"/>
  <text x="60" y="452" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">Lifetime prevalence  ·  IHME Global Burden of Disease 2025</text>
  <text x="60" y="472" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF">Higher lifetime risk driven by hormonal, psychosocial, and</text>
  <text x="60" y="490" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF">socioeconomic vulnerability factors</text>

  <!-- RIGHT CALLOUT — 1 in 5 Men -->
  <rect x="630" y="128" width="610" height="360" fill="#EFF6FF" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="630" y="128" width="5" height="360" fill="#1E40AF" rx="2"/>

  <!-- Icon placeholder -->
  <use data-icon="person" x="650" y="145" width="32" height="32" fill="#1E40AF"/>

  <text x="655" y="185" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF" letter-spacing="1">MEN</text>

  <!-- Big callout number -->
  <text x="890" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="128" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF" fill-opacity="0.12">5</text>
  <text x="680" y="295" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="76" font-weight="bold" fill="#0D1117">1 in 5</text>

  <text x="650" y="342" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#374151">men will experience</text>
  <text x="650" y="368" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">major depression</text>
  <text x="650" y="394" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#374151">in their lifetime</text>

  <rect x="650" y="420" width="565" height="1" fill="#DBEAFE"/>
  <text x="650" y="452" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">Lifetime prevalence  ·  IHME Global Burden of Disease 2025</text>
  <text x="650" y="472" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF">Risk is not limited to high-income settings — mental illness</text>
  <text x="650" y="490" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF">affects people across all countries and income levels</text>

  <!-- Bottom context box -->
  <rect x="40" y="506" width="1200" height="130" fill="#F9FAFB" rx="6"/>
  <rect x="40" y="506" width="5" height="130" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="60" y="533" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Why This Matters for Policy</text>
  <text x="60" y="558" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">Mental health conditions span from highly common (depression, anxiety) to less prevalent but profoundly severe (schizophrenia,</text>
  <text x="60" y="578" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">bipolar disorder). Hundreds of millions suffer each year; many more across their lifetimes. Despite effective treatments existing,</text>
  <text x="60" y="598" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">most people do not receive adequate care — making this a critical target for evidence-based public health investment.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="651" x2="1240" y2="651" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="682" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Our World in Data — Dattani, Rodés-Guirao, Ritchie & Roser (2023) / IHME GBD 2025</text>
  <text x="640" y="682" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="682" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6B7280">2</text>
</svg>

  <rect x="40" y="14" width="5" height="58" fill="#D4AF37"/>

  <!-- Sub-header -->
  <text x="40" y="100" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">DALYs per 100,000 people  ·  World  ·  2023  ·  In context against depression/anxiety</text>
  <line x1="40" y1="112" x2="1240" y2="112" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- LEFT CARD: Schizophrenia -->
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="580" height="390" fill="#F8FAFC" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="5" height="390" fill="#475569" rx="2"/>

  <text x="65" y="160" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#475569" letter-spacing="0.5">SCHIZOPHRENIA</text>
  <line x1="65" y1="170" x2="590" y2="170" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- Big DALY number -->
  <text x="310" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="88" font-weight="bold" fill="#475569">210.2</text>
  <text x="310" y="290" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#6B7280">DALYs per 100,000 people</text>

  <!-- Context comparison bar (small) -->
  <!-- Depression = 694.6, Schizophrenia = 210.2 → ratio = 30.3% -->
  <text x="65" y="325" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">vs. Depressive disorders (694.6):</text>
  <rect x="65" y="335" width="500" height="20" fill="#E2E8F0" rx="4"/>
  <rect x="65" y="335" width="151" height="20" fill="#475569" rx="4"/>
  <text x="228" y="350" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">30.3%</text>
  <text x="580" y="350" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">210.2 / 694.6</text>

  <!-- Key insight bullets -->
  <text x="65" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">▪ Profound disability</text>
  <text x="65" y="412" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  Positive symptoms (psychosis), negative symptoms, and</text>
  <text x="65" y="430" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  cognitive impairment combine to create severe burden</text>
  <text x="65" y="455" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">▪ Early onset, lifelong trajectory</text>
  <text x="65" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  Typically onset in late teens/early twenties; requires</text>
  <text x="65" y="495" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  long-term specialist care and community support</text>

  <!-- RIGHT CARD: Bipolar -->
  <rect x="650" y="122" width="590" height="390" fill="#F8FAFC" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="650" y="122" width="5" height="390" fill="#9CA3AF" rx="2"/>

  <text x="675" y="160" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#64748B" letter-spacing="0.5">BIPOLAR DISORDER</text>
  <line x1="675" y1="170" x2="1210" y2="170" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>

  <text x="945" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="88" font-weight="bold" fill="#9CA3AF">94.6</text>
  <text x="945" y="290" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#6B7280">DALYs per 100,000 people</text>

  <text x="675" y="325" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">vs. Depressive disorders (694.6):</text>
  <rect x="675" y="335" width="500" height="20" fill="#E2E8F0" rx="4"/>
  <!-- 94.6/694.6 = 13.6% → 500 * 0.136 = 68px -->
  <rect x="675" y="335" width="68" height="20" fill="#9CA3AF" rx="4"/>
  <text x="731" y="350" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">13.6%</text>
  <text x="1190" y="350" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">94.6 / 694.6</text>

  <text x="675" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">▪ Episodic but functionally disabling</text>
  <text x="675" y="412" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  Cycles of mania/hypomania and depression impair</text>
  <text x="675" y="430" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  occupational and social functioning even between episodes</text>
  <text x="675" y="455" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">▪ Often underdiagnosed</text>
  <text x="675" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  Frequently misdiagnosed as depression before bipolar</text>
  <text x="675" y="495" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">  features become apparent; delayed treatment is common</text>

  <!-- Proportion strip at bottom -->
  <text x="40" y="532" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151" font-weight="bold">Disease burden in context (all 5 categories):</text>
  <!-- Total = 694.6+686.5+210.2+94.6+47.5 = 1733.4 -->
  <!-- Proportions × 1200: Dep=480.4, Anx=475, Schiz=145.3, Bip=65.4, Eat=32.9 -->
  <rect x="40" y="543" width="481" height="26" fill="#1E40AF" rx="0"/>
  <rect x="521" y="543" width="475" height="26" fill="#00796B" rx="0"/>
  <rect x="996" y="543" width="145" height="26" fill="#475569" rx="0"/>
  <rect x="1141" y="543" width="65" height="26" fill="#9CA3AF" rx="0"/>
  <rect x="1206" y="543" width="34" height="26" fill="#CBD5E1" rx="0"/>
  <!-- Labels inside strip -->
  <text x="280" y="562" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">Depression 40.1%</text>
  <text x="758" y="562" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF" font-weight="bold">Anxiety 39.6%</text>
  <text x="1068" y="562" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#FFFFFF">Schiz. 12.1%</text>
  <text x="1173" y="562" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="9" fill="#FFFFFF">Bip. 5.5%</text>
  <text x="1223" y="562" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="8" fill="#6B7280">E.</text>

  <!-- Policy implication -->
  <rect x="40" y="577" width="1200" height="58" fill="#FEF9EC" rx="4"/>
  <rect x="40" y="577" width="5" height="58" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="58" y="601" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#92400E">Policy implication:</text>
  <text x="58" y="621" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#92400E">While schizophrenia and bipolar carry a smaller share of population-level DALYs, their per-person severity demands specialized, sustained care systems — not just primary care scaling.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="647" x2="1240" y2="647" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="682" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: IHME GBD 2025 / Our World in Data — Dattani et al. (2023)</text>
  <text x="640" y="682" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="682" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6B7280">5</text>
</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#00796B"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="url(#topGrad)"/>

  <!-- Exhibit Takeaway Bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="1200" height="58" fill="#0D1117" rx="2"/>
  <rect x="40" y="14" width="5" height="58" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="58" y="51" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" letter-spacing="0.5">Treatment Is Available but Often Lacking or of Poor Quality — A Large Gap Persists Globally</text>

  <!-- Opening statement -->
  <rect x="40" y="84" width="1200" height="36" fill="#F0FDF4" rx="4"/>
  <text x="58" y="108" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#065F46">Mental illnesses <tspan font-weight="bold">are treatable</tspan>. Yet across all income settings, many people do not receive adequate care — or any care at all.</text>

  <line x1="40" y1="130" x2="1240" y2="130" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- Section label -->
  <text x="640" y="158" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151" letter-spacing="1">FOUR KEY BARRIERS TO TREATMENT</text>

  <!-- 2x2 grid of barrier cards -->
  <!-- Card 1: Stigma (top-left) -->
  <rect x="40" y="170" width="575" height="200" fill="#FEF2F2" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="170" width="5" height="200" fill="#DC2626" rx="2"/>
  <!-- Icon -->
  <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="65" y="190" width="40" height="40" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="120" y="215" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">STIGMA</text>
  <line x1="65" y1="228" x2="585" y2="228" stroke="#FECACA" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="65" y="254" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">Many people are uncomfortable disclosing mental</text>
  <text x="65" y="274" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">health symptoms to healthcare professionals or even</text>
  <text x="65" y="294" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">to people they know.</text>
  <text x="65" y="322" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">Stigma suppresses help-seeking and distorts prevalence data</text>
  <text x="65" y="340" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">— the true burden is likely higher than reported.</text>
  <text x="65" y="360" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">   </text>

  <!-- Card 2: Access (top-right) -->
  <rect x="640" y="170" width="600" height="200" fill="#FFF7ED" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="640" y="170" width="5" height="200" fill="#EA580C" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="lock-closed" x="665" y="190" width="40" height="40" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="720" y="215" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#EA580C">ACCESS BARRIERS</text>
  <line x1="665" y1="228" x2="1210" y2="228" stroke="#FED7AA" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="665" y="254" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">Treatment is often lacking, especially in low- and</text>
  <text x="665" y="274" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">middle-income countries where mental health systems</text>
  <text x="665" y="294" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">are severely underfunded.</text>
  <text x="665" y="322" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">Geographic, financial, and systemic barriers prevent</text>
  <text x="665" y="342" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">millions from reaching trained mental health providers.</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Quality (bottom-left) -->
  <rect x="40" y="388" width="575" height="200" fill="#F0F9FF" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="388" width="5" height="200" fill="#0369A1" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="shield" x="65" y="408" width="40" height="40" fill="#0369A1"/>
  <text x="120" y="432" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#0369A1">QUALITY GAPS</text>
  <line x1="65" y1="445" x2="585" y2="445" stroke="#BAE6FD" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="65" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">Even where treatment exists, it may be of poor</text>
  <text x="65" y="490" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">quality — underdosed medications, inadequate</text>
  <text x="65" y="510" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">psychotherapy, or untrained providers.</text>
  <text x="65" y="538" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">Receiving some care is not the same as receiving</text>
  <text x="65" y="558" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">effective, evidence-based care.</text>

  <!-- Card 4: Underreporting (bottom-right) -->
  <rect x="640" y="388" width="600" height="200" fill="#F5F3FF" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="640" y="388" width="5" height="200" fill="#7C3AED" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="magnifying-glass" x="665" y="408" width="40" height="40" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <text x="720" y="432" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">UNDERREPORTING</text>
  <line x1="665" y1="445" x2="1210" y2="445" stroke="#DDD6FE" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="665" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">Discomfort with disclosure makes it difficult to</text>
  <text x="665" y="490" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">accurately estimate the true prevalence of mental</text>
  <text x="665" y="510" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#374151">illness — actual burden is likely underestimated.</text>
  <text x="665" y="538" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">Good data is essential: how, when, and why conditions</text>
  <text x="665" y="558" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#9CA3AF" font-style="italic">occur, and how many people are truly affected.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="602" x2="1240" y2="602" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="682" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Our World in Data — Dattani et al. (2023) / IHME GBD 2025</text>
  <text x="640" y="682" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="682" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#6B7280">6</text>
</svg>

  <!-- Card 1: Prescribed Medication -->
  <rect x="40" y="158" width="370" height="370" fill="#EFF6FF" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="40" y="158" width="5" height="370" fill="#1E40AF" rx="2"/>
